1.1.title: Establish and Maintain Detailed Enterprise Asset Inventory
1.1.description: Establish and maintain an accurate, detailed, and up-to-date inventory of all enterprise assets with the potential to store or process data, to include: end-user devices (including portable and mobile), network devices, non-computing/IoT devices, and servers. Ensure the inventory records the network address (if static), hardware address, machine name, enterprise asset owner, department for each asset, and whether the asset has been approved to connect to the network. For mobile end-user devices, MDM type tools can support this process, where appropriate. This inventory includes assets connected to the infrastructure physically, virtually, remotely, and those within cloud environments. Additionally, it includes assets that are regularly connected to the enterprise’s network infrastructure, even if they are not under control of the enterprise. Review and update the inventory of all enterprise assets bi-annually, or more frequently.

3.8.title: Document Data Flows
3.8.description: Document data flows. Data flow documentation includes service provider data flows and should be based on the enterprise’s data management process. Review and update documentation annually, or when significant enterprise changes occur that could impact this Safeguard.

3.12.title: Segment Data Processing and Storage Based on Sensitivity
3.12.description: Segment data processing and storage based on the sensitivity of the data. Do not process sensitive data on enterprise assets intended for lower sensitivity data.

4.4.title: Implement and Manage a Firewall on Servers
4.4.description: Implement and manage a firewall on servers, where supported. Example implementations include a virtual firewall, operating system firewall, or a third-party firewall agent.

4.9.title: Configure Trusted DNS Servers on Enterprise Assets
4.9.description: Configure trusted DNS servers on network infrastructure. Example implementations include configuring network devices to use enterprise-controlled DNS servers and/or reputable externally accessible DNS servers.

6.4.title: Require MFA for Remote Network Access
6.4.description: Require MFA for remote network access.

9.2.title: Use DNS Filtering Services
9.2.description: Use DNS filtering services on all end-user devices, including remote and on-premises assets, to block access to known malicious domains.

9.3.title: Maintain and Enforce Network-Based URL Filters
9.3.description: Enforce and update network-based URL filters to limit an enterprise asset from connecting to potentially malicious or unapproved websites. Example implementations include category-based filtering, reputation-based filtering, or through the use of block lists. Enforce filters for all enterprise assets.

12.2.title: Establish and Maintain a Secure Network Architecture
12.2.description: Design and maintain a secure network architecture. A secure network architecture must address segmentation, least privilege, and availability, at a minimum. Example implementations may include documentation, policy, and design components.

12.3.title: Securely Manage Network Infrastructure
12.3.description: Securely manage network infrastructure. Example implementations include version-controlled Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC), and the use of secure network protocols, such as SSH and HTTPS.

12.5.title: Centralize Network Authentication, Authorization, and Auditing (AAA)

12.7.title: Ensure Remote Devices Utilize a VPN and are Connecting to an Enterprise’s AAA Infrastructure
12.7.description: Require users to authenticate to enterprise-managed VPN and authentication services prior to accessing enterprise resources on end-user devices.

12.8.title: Establish and Maintain Dedicated Computing Resources for All Administrative Work
12.8.description: Establish and maintain dedicated computing resources, either physically or logically separated, for all administrative tasks or tasks requiring administrative access. The computing resources should be segmented from the enterprise's primary network and not be allowed internet access.

13.3.title: Deploy a Network Intrusion Detection Solution
13.3.description: Deploy a network intrusion detection solution on enterprise assets, where appropriate. Example implementations include the use of a Network Intrusion Detection System (NIDS) or equivalent cloud service provider (CSP) service.

13.4.title: Perform Traffic Filtering Between Network Segments
13.4.description: Perform traffic filtering between network segments, where appropriate.

13.5.title: Manage Access Control for Remote Assets
13.5.description: Manage access control for assets remotely connecting to enterprise resources. Determine amount of access to enterprise resources based on: up-to-date anti-malware software installed, configuration compliance with the enterprise’s secure configuration process, and ensuring the operating system and applications are up-to-date.

13.6.title: Collect Network Traffic Flow Logs
13.6.description: Collect network traffic flow logs and/or network traffic to review and alert upon from network devices.

13.8.title: Deploy a Network Intrusion Prevention Solution
13.8.description: Deploy a network intrusion prevention solution, where appropriate. Example implementations include the use of a Network Intrusion Prevention System (NIPS) or equivalent CSP service.

13.9.title: Deploy Port-Level Access Control
13.9.description: Deploy port-level access control. Port-level access control utilizes 802.1x, or similar network access control protocols, such as certificates, and may incorporate user and/or device authentication.

13.10.title: Perform Application Layer Filtering
13.10.description: Perform application layer filtering. Example implementations include a filtering proxy, application layer firewall, or gateway.

16.8.title: Separate Production and Non-Production Systems
16.8.description: Maintain separate environments for production and non-production systems.

18.2.title: Perform Periodic External Penetration Tests
18.2.description: Perform periodic external penetration tests based on program requirements, no less than annually. External penetration testing must include enterprise and environmental reconnaissance to detect exploitable information. Penetration testing requires specialized skills and experience and must be conducted through a qualified party. The testing may be clear box or opaque box.
